elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered carve-out: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets." The affiliate transfer sits inside the express exception to the prior-written-consent sentence, so no IBM consent is required.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same carve-out expressly lists "a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" and operates "[n]otwithstanding the foregoing" consent requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "IBM will not assign this Agreement without Customer's prior written consent..." — the restriction now binds the Vendor symmetrically.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Added sentence carries the standard: "...without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld..."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and will not assign to a competitor of Customer." The bar is absolute and is not qualified by any consent, successor, or affiliate exception, so it operates as a never-permitted assignment.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "A change of control of Customer will not give IBM any right to terminate this Agreement." Confirmatory (no such right existed in p0188), but it is operative language, not merely a comment promise.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Customer has a successor carve-out, but the new IBM sentence subjects every IBM assignment—including to a successor—to Customer's prior written consent, with no successor exception. Not required, since the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Neither the retained nor the added language imposes any notice obligation for a successor assignment.
The retained/widened "Notwithstanding" sentence permits assignment to an affiliate without consent — a no-consent non-successor exception, which under the ASSIGN fallback rule defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Both the retained Customer-side sentence and the new IBM-side sentence carry "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld."

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete in operative text: the existing Customer carve-out is widened to affiliates and sales of substantially all assets, and a new reciprocal sentence supplies Vendor-side consent, the reasonableness standard, the absolute competitor bar, and the no-change-of-control-termination confirmation. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation because the original bound only Customer and left IBM free to assign to anyone, including our competitor.

Minimality holds: no words were deleted, the general consent sentence, the void-assignment sentence and the continuing-liability sentence are all retained verbatim, and the edits are confined to the six preferred elements. The "Notwithstanding the foregoing" construction was already in the original clause and was not newly added as a broad override, so the anti-override guidance is not triggered.
No extras were bolted on — no survival tail, no notice mechanic, no re-pricing or change-of-control definition, no damages or procedural language beyond the checklist.

Intent is preserved: the reciprocal IBM sentence does not contradict the retained Customer-side sentence, no cross-reference is broken, and no Vendor-favourable new assignment exception was created (the affiliate/asset-sale carve-out runs to Customer only).

Minor drafting note only, not a defect requiring repair: "affiliate" and "competitor of Customer" are used without definition. If the Base Terms do not define "Affiliate," consider a short parenthetical (e.g., "an entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with Customer") to avoid an interpretive fight; this does not affect element coverage.

Fallback level is not independently satisfied (no written-notice mechanic, no IBM successor right, and the affiliate carve-out defeats "other assignments require consent"), but that is immaterial because completeness at the preferred level is sufficient.
